name: The hamzated verb (mahmūz)
definition: A verb with a hamza among its root letters: first (akhadha), middle (saʾala) or last (qaraʾa).
body: The hamza counts as a sound letter but is softened or dropped in some forms. Three verbs with a first hamza lose it in the imperative, by a usage the books take from the Arabs: khudh from akhadha, kul from akala and mur from amara. A middle hamza may drop and give its vowel to the letter before it, as in sal, an imperative of saʾala; a final one makes the verb behave in places like a defective.

examples.text: khudh, kul, mur: the imperatives of akhadha, akala and amara, without their hamza.
